title: Events, modifiers and callbacks between components

videos.script:
In Svelte 5, an event handler is just an attribute. {{attr}} onclick, oninput, onsubmit. Its value is a function, and that is all there is to learn about the syntax.

What there is to learn is which element to put it on. {{form}} The planner's add form becomes a real form. Enter submits it, the browser checks the fields, and a screen reader announces it properly.

Then the modifiers Svelte 4 had. {{mods}} They are gone, and each one is now a line in the handler, where you can read it.

Then the keyboard. {{keys}} A clickable list item, and the two warnings the compiler gives you for it. And a shortcut for the week that stays out of the way while you type.

And last, components talking to each other. {{callbacks}} A child reports what happened by calling a function its parent gave it. A few conventions keep those calls easy to read.
